speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the nature of your flank pain and confirm if you have experienced any changes in your urination, such as frequency or burning? Also, have you had a fever since finishing your antibiotics?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain or burning sensation when you urinate, and have you noticed any blood in your urine? I also need to know if you have had any chills or night sweats accompanying the fever.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: It sounds like you may have developed an allergic reaction, specifically acute interstitial nephritis, triggered by the antibiotics. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and serum creatinine.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Serum Creatinine: Elevated. Urinalysis with microscopy: Leukocyturia present, Bacterial Culture negative, Cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution shows 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm (consistent with eosinophils).

text: RESULTS: Serum Creatinine: Elevated. Urinalysis with microscopy: Leukocyturia present, Bacterial Culture negative, Cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution shows 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm (consistent with eosinophils).

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in the urine and elevated creatinine strongly supports my suspicion. I will now request renal ultrasound images to assess kidney structure and rule out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the rash, fever, eosinophiluria, and elevated creatinine following antibiotic use, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
